proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every finite revealed graph \(G\), an exact draw from \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) can be generated in randomized time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\). Finite enumeration of the capped latent sample space computes every \(\pi_u\) and detects whether any \(\pi_u\) is zero. If every \(\pi_u>0\), the same enumeration computes every entry of \(\Gamma_G\), evaluates \(\widetilde\tau_G\) on every latent atom, and computes every conditional weight and value defining \(\widehat\tau_G\) on each positive-probability observed-data atom. Under this positivity condition, \(\widehat\tau_G\) is a finite measurable observed-data function and is exactly auditable without observing internal focal metadata. Exact enumeration is not asserted to run in polynomial time.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unconditional estimator-totality claim is false. For the admissible smallest instance \(n=4\), \(d=3\), and \(G=K_4\), one has \(k=1\) and \(F_G(A)=\varnothing\) for every singleton \(A\); the fallback is certain and every \(\pi_u=0\). Enumeration always detects this case, but the normalized kernel and the positive-inclusion estimator formulas may be evaluated only after positivity is verified.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Can the local handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be developed into an algorithm running in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\) that evaluates or approximates \(\widehat\tau_G\) from \((G,Z^{\mathrm{cap}},y(Z^{\mathrm{cap}}))\), and returns an observable certificate \(U_G\) satisfying \[\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]\le U_G?\] Can such a certificate either establish \(U_G=O(r(n,d))\) on a probability-\(1-o(1)\) random-regular graph event, or furnish a rigorous obstruction to \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\), while numerical approximation error contributes \(o(r(n,d))\)? If a balanced-hole lower edge at scale \(r(n,d)\) is separately established, an affirmative compiler and \(O(n/k)\) certificate could potentially close the resulting logarithmic bracket for \(R_2(G)\) and make the capsule deployable; it would not implement an already established matched minimax theorem. Both the polynomial-time algorithmic construction and the capsule spectral bound remain open, and the proved upper bound uses a different published Conflict Graph Design.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unqualified supremum ranges beyond the frozen endpoint-\(L^2\) ANI class and is not the paper's risk claim. The consumer also overstated what a compiler would implement: the capsule norm bound and the strengthened random-regular lower edge require separate proofs.

proposed.comparator_claim: For random \(d\)-regular \(G\) with \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), the published growing-degree bracket is \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) with probability \(1-o(1)\).

Lemma 3.3 gives closed-form desired-exposure probabilities, Lemma 4.2 gives local covariance bounds, and Theorem 4.1 bounds modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by \(12.5\lambda(H_G)/n\) times the two endpoint empirical second moments after the GATE spectral identification.
The neighborhood-union construction gives a one-sided treated-component upper bound under controlled codegrees and leaves the full estimator open.
A greedy independent focal set has size at least \(n\log s/s\) with high probability in the paper's Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi regime.
Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 compare uniform root mean-squared error of a design-based Riesz estimator with the scaled norm of its variance operator.
The largest balanced independent sets in generic random bipartite graphs have density \((2+o_d(1))\log d/d\), with a factor-two local-algorithm barrier.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The unaudited strengthened random-regular lower edge cannot be positioned as a strict tightening of the published minimax bracket; the comparator table must record only the supported equivalence until the balanced-hole estimate is proved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a polynomial-time observed-data approximation to \(\widehat\tau_G\) and an observable operator-norm risk certificate valid uniformly over \(y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\), with numerical contribution \(o(r(n,d))\); separately prove \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\) on the required random-regular event or certify an obstruction.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact enumeration is finite but exponential. Simulation error bounds depend on an inverse-polynomial lower bound for \(\min_u\pi_u\), while simulation of the Rao--Blackwell ratio also depends on the probability of the realized assignment fiber. Neither lower bound, nor a contraction, mixing-time, approximate-counting, or deterministic spectral certificate, is supplied by the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: I extended the finite-enumeration reduction with simultaneous Chebyshev bounds for all inclusion and joint-inclusion probabilities and an explicit entrywise-to-operator-norm conversion. This gives pointwise approximation when positive overlap is quantitatively known, but does not control the conditional Rao--Blackwell fiber or furnish the required uniform polynomial bound.

prose_updates.tldr: For fixed potential outcomes under arbitrary neighborhood interference on a revealed random \(d\)-regular graph, the fully audited unconditional comparison is the published-order bracket: uniformly for feasible \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), with probability \(1-o(1)\), \(c(d+1)/n\le R_2(G)\le C(1+d^2)/n\). For fixed \(d\), this gives \(R_2(G)=\Theta_d(n^{-1})\). The proposed stronger lower edge \(r(n,d)=(d+1)^2/[n\log(d+2)]\) still requires a valid random-regular balanced-hole theorem. The reservoir capsule has exact covariance identities and an exact finite audit conditional on positive focal inclusion, but its \(O(n/k)\) norm bound, scalable compiler, and logarithmically improved risk remain open.

project_justification.gap: Published unrestricted minimax theory places growing-degree random-regular full-GATE risk between orders \(d/n\) and \(d^2/n\). A deterministic balanced-hole Bayes reduction can identify the graph certificate needed for the stronger lower scale, but the required uniform random-regular switching comparison has not been proved or anchored by a matching primary theorem.
project_justification.niche: The two-copy exposure graph and balanced reservoir capsule expose exact covariance structure and a concrete computational target. They isolate two unresolved tasks: the accepted compatible-pair operator bound and a polynomial-time observed-data compiler with auditable error.
project_justification.fill: The paper retains the supported all-procedure lower comparison and the observed-data adaptation of the published conflict-graph upper design, records the \(\Theta_d(n^{-1})\) fixed-degree benchmark, proves the capsule's exact finite covariance algebra, and supplies a finite evaluator that detects zero inclusion before computing kernel or estimator formulas. It does not claim an exact frontier or capsule attainment.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on the revealed \(G\), the proved upper guarantee uses the outcome-independent published Conflict Graph Design and an observed-data Rao--Blackwellized modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator. The capped balanced reservoir law \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) is a separate candidate whose sharper covariance rate and scalable evaluation are open.
sampling_model.units: The finite population \(V\) and its potential-outcome schedule are fixed conditional on \(G\); assignment is the only inferential randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Both designs generate one binary assignment. The published design resolves requested endpoint exposures by a conflict-graph importance ordering; the capsule forces the closed neighborhoods of its two focal reservoirs to opposite arms and randomizes the remainder.
sampling_model.overlap: The published design's desired-exposure probabilities are explicitly positive under its closed-form construction. The finite capsule evaluator always computes and checks every \(\pi_u\); uniform order-\(k/n\) capsule overlap is unresolved and is never presumed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no super-population nuisances. Published desired-exposure weights have closed forms. When every capsule inclusion probability is positive, capsule inclusions, covariance entries, and Rao--Blackwell weights are exact finite-design functionals computable by enumeration; enumeration may be exponential and polynomial-time uniform approximation remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje define the same endpoint-\(L^2\) unrestricted minimax experiment and prove the growing-degree random-regular bracket \(d/n\lesssim R_2(G)\lesssim d^2/n\) under \(d=o(\sqrt n)\). The attempted strengthening of its lower edge to \(r(n,d)\) reduces to a balanced-hole estimate, but the needed simple-random-regular switching counts are not yet verified. Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw provide the closed upper route used here: Lemma 3.3 gives exact desired-exposure probabilities, Lemma 4.2 controls local normalized covariances, and Theorem 4.1 gives the \(O(\lambda(H_G)/n)\) modified Horvitz--Thompson variance bound. Li and Li prove only a treated-component result. Harshaw, S\"avje, and Wang motivate operator-norm risk analysis, while Perkins and Wang and Cai, Zhang, and Airoldi study balanced or independent sets in different graph and estimand settings; none supplies the acceptance-conditioned two-arm capsule covariance estimate or compiler required here.
prose_updates.interpretation: The supported bracket rules out risk below the published lower order and gives the ordinary \(n^{-1}\) benchmark at every fixed degree, but it does not determine the growing-degree frontier. A valid balanced-hole theorem would strengthen the all-procedure lower edge to \(r(n,d)\). Independently, an \(O(n/k)\) capsule norm certificate would yield a sharper observed-data upper construction. Both advances remain separate obligations.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Two nontrivial steps remain unresolved. First, the proposed random-regular balanced-hole estimate needs uniform switching counts that explicitly control simple-graph invalid moves, exceptional internal-edge strata, and the available half-edge event. Second, the capsule's accepted compatible-pair covariance block contains the random denominator \(\binom{|F_G(A)|}{k}\), and neither entrywise bounds nor pointwise Monte Carlo supplies the required operator-norm certificate or efficient conditional Rao--Blackwell weights. No switching, covariance, overlap, or computational premise is added to assume either crux.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper does not prove the strengthened random-regular lower edge, an exact minimax frontier, or capsule attainment at \(d^2/[n\log d]\). It does prove or retain the supported published-order bracket and the fixed-degree \(\Theta_d(n^{-1})\) benchmark. The capsule assignment law is total, but its normalized kernel and estimator audit are asserted only after finite enumeration verifies every \(\pi_u>0\); \(G=K_4\) at \(n=4\) is an explicit zero-inclusion witness. Exact enumeration may be exponential, and scalable certification remains open. No studentized central limit theorem, bounded-outcome model, additive interference model, or real-network random-regular approximation is claimed.
prose_updates.estimand_functional: Uniformly for feasible \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), \(c(d+1)/n\le R_2(G)\le C(1+d^2)/n\) with probability \(1-o(1)\), and \(R_2(G)=\Theta_d(n^{-1})\) for fixed \(d\). The upper bound is attained by the published Conflict Graph Design after observed-data Rao--Blackwellization. The stronger lower scale \(r(n,d)\), the capsule upper bound at that scale, and a polynomial-time capsule compiler remain open.
